I expanded the marker — the whole log was behind it, so there was nothing I could say without doing that. Here's what's actually in the 332 lines.

## First, a caveat about the "no match" claim

You didn't tell me which dependency the agent cares about, so I can't confirm or refute the marker. And there's a structural reason to be suspicious of a bare "no match" here: **every `Compiling` line in this log is for an `@`-scoped package**, running alphabetically from `@babel/code-frame` to `@vitest/utils`. Unscoped packages get no line of their own. They appear *only* inside parenthetical peer annotations:

```
@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.30.0(zod v4.5.4)
@hono/node-server@2.1.1(hono v4.13.5)
@vitest/mocker@4.1.11(vite@8.2.2(@types/node@26.4.0)(esbuild@0.28.2)(jiti v2.7.0))
```

So if the focus term was `vite`, `zod`, `hono`, `jiti`, `lightningcss`, `react`, `typescript`, `esbuild`, `rollup`, `oxlint`, or `vitest`, a scan keyed on `Compiling <name>` would report "not found" while the dependency is very much in the tree. Tell me the name and I'll give you a definitive answer.

## What the log says

- **Build succeeded.** `Finished \`dev\` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s), 327 units`. Zero errors, zero warnings, no `error[E…]`, no retries.
- **It's synthetic.** The header says so outright: generated by `bench/gen-build-log.mjs` from the repo's `pnpm-lock.yaml`; package names/versions are real, the cargo framing is not. Don't read build *timing* or *ordering* into it.
- **Two passes.** A plain alphabetical list, then a second pass over roughly the same set with peer-dependency annotations attached.

## Things worth flagging regardless of your target

1. **Two major versions of vite coexist.** `vite@7.3.6(@types/node@24.13.3)(jiti@2.7.0)(lightningcss v1.33.0)` backs `@tailwindcss/vite` and `@vitejs/plugin-react`, while `vite@8.2.2(@types/node@26.4.0)(esbuild@0.28.2)(jiti v2.7.0)` backs `@vitest/mocker`.
